subproblem.title: Upper semicontinuity of the slice length (Simon's note to 2.10)
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. For y ∈ ℝ^d let λ(y) := (L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A})).toReal, where y[j↦t] is y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)) and L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Then λ : ℝ^d → ℝ is upper semicontinuous: for every x ∈ ℝ^d and every real r > λ(x) there is a neighbourhood N of x with λ(y) < r for all y ∈ N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → UpperSemicontinuous (fun y : Euclid d => (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon's note after the proof of 2.10 and parent step 1c (choose an open U ⊇ A_ξ with L¹(U) ≤ λ(ξ) + ε and use the compactness of A). The parent's subsequence argument is written here as the closedness of a compact projection. Notation: A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, y[j↦t] = WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t), λ(y) = (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal. In Mathlib, UpperSemicontinuous λ means: for all x and r with λ(x) < r, eventually for y in 𝓝 x, λ(y) < r.
1. Slices have finite measure. A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R; for t ∈ A^j_y, |t| ≤ ‖y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so A^j_y ⊆ [−R, R] and L¹(A^j_y) ≤ L¹([−R, R]) < ∞. Hence ofReal(λ(y)) = L¹(A^j_y) for every y (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
2. Fix x ∈ ℝ^d and r > λ(x). Then L¹(A^j_x) = ofReal(λ(x)) < ofReal(r) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff_of_nonneg). By outer regularity of Lebesgue measure on ℝ there is an open set U ⊇ A^j_x with L¹(U) < ofReal(r) (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt).
3. Let O := {z ∈ ℝ^d : z_j ∈ U}, open as the preimage of U under the continuous coordinate map z ↦ z_j, and C := A ∖ O, compact as a closed subset of the compact set A (IsCompact.diff). Let π(z) := z[j↦0]; π is continuous, so π(C) is compact and hence closed.
4. Same projection. If π(z) = π(y), then z = y[j↦z_j]: for i ≠ j, z_i = (π z)_i = (π y)_i = y_i, and the j-th coordinates of both sides equal z_j. Moreover π(y[j↦t]) = π(y) for all t.
5. π(x) ∉ π(C). Otherwise π(z) = π(x) for some z ∈ C ⊆ A; by step 4, x[j↦z_j] = z ∈ A, so z_j ∈ A^j_x ⊆ U, i.e. z ∈ O, contradicting z ∈ C = A ∖ O.
6. Hence N := π⁻¹(ℝ^d ∖ π(C)) is open (continuity of π) and contains x, so it is a neighbourhood of x. For y ∈ N we have A^j_y ⊆ U: if t ∈ A^j_y but t ∉ U, then z := y[j↦t] ∈ A with z_j = t ∉ U, so z ∈ C, and π(z) = π(y) by step 4, so π(y) ∈ π(C), contradicting y ∈ N.
7. For y ∈ N: L¹(A^j_y) ≤ L¹(U) < ofReal(r), hence λ(y) = (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal < r (ENNReal.toReal_lt_of_lt_ofReal). Thus λ(y) < r on the neighbourhood N of x; since x and r were arbitrary, λ is upper semicontinuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: Slices lie in [−R, R], so ofReal(λ y) = L¹(A^j_y) < ∞.
Outer regularity gives an open U ⊇ A^j_x with L¹(U) < ofReal r.
C := A ∖ {z : z_j ∈ U} is compact; its projection π(C), π(z) = z[j↦0], is closed and does not contain π(x).
On the neighbourhood π⁻¹(π(C)ᶜ) of x every slice lies in U, so λ < r there.

subproblem.title: Steiner symmetrization of a compact set is compact
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. Let A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, where y[j↦t] is y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)), and λ(y) := (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal. If λ : ℝ^d → ℝ is upper semicontinuous, then the Steiner symmetrization S_j(A) := {y ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2} is compact.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → UpperSemicontinuous (fun y : Euclid d => (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal) → IsCompact {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1c and Simon's note after 2.10 (S_j(A) is compact because the slice length is upper semicontinuous); the upper semicontinuity is the hypothesis. Notation: A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, y[j↦t] = WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t), λ(y) = (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal, π(z) := z[j↦0].
1. π is continuous; π(y[j↦t]) = π(y) for all t; and π(z) = π(y) implies z = y[j↦z_j] (the coordinates with index i ≠ j agree, and both j-th coordinates equal z_j).
2. N := {y : A^j_y ≠ ∅} equals π⁻¹(π(A)). If t ∈ A^j_y, then y[j↦t] ∈ A and π(y[j↦t]) = π(y), so π(y) ∈ π(A). Conversely, if π(z) = π(y) with z ∈ A, then y[j↦z_j] = z ∈ A by step 1, so z_j ∈ A^j_y. Since π(A) is compact (continuous image of a compact set), it is closed, so N is closed.
3. M := {y : |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2} is closed. The function f(y) := λ(y) + (−2|y_j|) is upper semicontinuous as the sum of the upper semicontinuous λ and a continuous function (UpperSemicontinuous.add, Continuous.upperSemicontinuous). Superlevel sets of upper semicontinuous functions are closed (UpperSemicontinuous.isClosed_preimage: f⁻¹([0, ∞)) is closed), and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2 ⟺ 0 ≤ f(y), so M = f⁻¹([0, ∞)) is closed.
4. S_j(A) = N ∩ M (its defining condition is the conjunction of the two conditions; Set.ofPred_and), hence S_j(A) is closed.
5. S_j(A) is bounded. A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R. Let y ∈ S_j(A) and choose t ∈ A^j_y; then y[j↦t] ∈ A, so ‖y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R, and in particular R ≥ 0. Every s ∈ A^j_y satisfies |s| ≤ ‖y[j↦s]‖ ≤ R (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so A^j_y ⊆ [−R, R], L¹(A^j_y) ≤ ofReal(2R) and λ(y) ≤ 2R; thus |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2 ≤ R, and |t| ≤ R. The vector y − y[j↦t] has j-th coordinate y_j − t and all other coordinates 0, so ‖y − y[j↦t]‖ = |y_j − t| (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence ‖y‖ ≤ ‖y[j↦t]‖ + ‖y − y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R + |y_j| + |t| ≤ 3R, i.e. S_j(A) ⊆ closedBall(0, 3R).
6. ℝ^d is a proper metric space, so the closed and bounded set S_j(A) is compact (isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). ∎
proof_key_steps: {y : A^j_y ≠ ∅} = π⁻¹(π(A)) with π(z) = z[j↦0] is closed.
{y : |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2} is the superlevel set {λ − 2|y_j| ≥ 0} of an upper semicontinuous function, hence closed.
Every y ∈ S_j(A) satisfies ‖y‖ ≤ 3R.
Closed and bounded in ℝ^d implies compact.

audit.reason: The type explicitly includes the upper-semicontinuity hypothesis used in the proof. The projection condition and superlevel condition are closed; the supplied 3R estimate proves boundedness. Properness then gives compactness, without requiring the slice_usc sibling.

subproblem.title: Steiner symmetrization does not increase the diameter
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. With y[j↦t] := y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)), A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, λ(y) := (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal and S_j(A) := {y ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2}, the extended diameters satisfy ediam S_j(A) ≤ ediam A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ediam {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2} ≤ ediam A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1e (Simon, proof of 2.10: S_j(A) has diameter not larger than that of A). Notation: y[j↦t] = WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t), y_j = y j; with ξ = y[j↦0], A^j_y is the parent's A_ξ and λ(y) = λ(ξ), so S_j(A) is the parent's set.
1. Slices are compact and uniformly bounded. A is bounded, so A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R (IsBounded.subset_closedBall). For y ∈ ℝ^d and t ∈ A^j_y: |t| = |(y[j↦t])_j| ≤ ‖y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so A^j_y ⊆ [−R, R]. A^j_y is the preimage of the closed set A under the continuous map t ↦ y[j↦t] (PiLp.continuous_toLp composed with Continuous.update), hence closed; being closed and bounded in ℝ, it is compact.
2. Length versus spread. Let P ⊆ ℝ be compact and nonempty, a := inf P, b := sup P. Then a, b ∈ P (IsCompact.sInf_mem, IsCompact.sSup_mem), a ≤ b and P ⊆ [a, b] (csInf_le, le_csSup), so L¹(P) ≤ L¹([a, b]) = ofReal(b − a) (Real.volume_Icc), hence (L¹(P)).toReal ≤ b − a.
3. Replacing one coordinate. For x, y ∈ ℝ^d and a, b ∈ ℝ: |x[j↦a] − y[j↦b]|² = |x − y|² − (x_j − y_j)² + (a − b)². Indeed |u − v|² = Σ_i (u_i − v_i)² (EuclideanSpace.dist_sq_eq); after splitting off the index j (Finset.sum_erase_add), the terms with i ≠ j coincide for (x, y) and (x[j↦a], y[j↦b]), while the j-th terms are (x_j − y_j)² and (a − b)².

subproblem.title: Isodiametric bound for centrally symmetric sets
subproblem.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ and every set K ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) such that −x ∈ K whenever x ∈ K (no measurability or boundedness assumed): L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d in [0, ∞]. Here L^d = volume, ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and ediam is the extended diameter.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid d)), (∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) → volume K ≤ unitBallVolume d * (ediam K / 2) ^ d
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: final step of Simon's proof of 2.10 / parent step 1g (the symmetrized set lies in the closed ball of radius ½ diam about 0, whence the bound). No measurability, compactness or boundedness of K is assumed.
1. ω_d ∈ (0, ∞): the open unit ball is a nonempty open set, so its volume is positive (Metric.measure_ball_pos for the additive Haar measure volume); it is bounded, so its volume is finite (measure_ball_lt_top).
2. Case ediam K = ∞. Then d ≥ 1: for d = 0, ℝ⁰ has exactly one point, so K is subsingleton and ediam K = 0 (ediam_subsingleton). For d ≥ 1, (∞/2)^d = ∞ (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top, ENNReal.top_pow) and ω_d·∞ = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top, ω_d ≠ 0), so the inequality holds trivially.
3. Case ediam K < ∞. Then K is bounded (isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top). For x ∈ K also −x ∈ K, so 2‖x‖ = ‖x − (−x)‖ = dist(x, −x) ≤ diam K (dist_le_diam_of_mem). Hence K ⊆ closedBall(0, r) with r := diam K/2 ≥ 0.
4. L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^d)·ω_d. By Measure.addHaar_closedBall for the additive Haar measure volume, L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^{finrank})·L^d(ball(0, 1)), and finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) = d (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). This holds for every d, including 0.
5. ofReal(r^d) = ofReal(r)^d = (ofReal(diam K)/2)^d = (ediam K/2)^d. This uses r ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pow), ofReal(a/2) = ofReal(a)/2 (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos), and ofReal(diam K) = ofReal((ediam K).toReal) = ediam K because ediam K ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
6. By monotonicity of measure, L^d(K) ≤ L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_d = unitBallVolume d is positive and finite.
ediam K = ∞ forces d ≥ 1 and an infinite right-hand side.
Central symmetry gives K ⊆ closedBall(0, diam K/2).
L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^d)·ω_d and ofReal(diam K/2)^d = (ediam K/2)^d.

subproblem.title: Iterated Steiner symmetrization gives a centrally symmetric compact replacement
subproblem.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ and every compact A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) there is a compact K ⊆ ℝ^d with L^d(K) = L^d(A) (L^d = volume), ediam K ≤ ediam A, and −x ∈ K for every x ∈ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ∃ K : Set (Euclid d), IsCompact K ∧ volume K = volume A ∧ ediam K ≤ ediam A ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1g (Simon 2.10: applying Steiner symmetrization successively with respect to the coordinate planes x¹ = 0, …, xⁿ = 0 gives a compact set Ã with diameter ≤ diam A, the same Lebesgue measure as A, and invariant under x ↦ −x).
Notation. For i ∈ Fin d, R_i(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp i (−y i)) is the reflection in x_i = 0. For B ⊆ ℝ^d, S_i(B) is the coordinate Steiner symmetrization of the sibling statements: the set {y | {t | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp i t) ∈ B}.Nonempty ∧ |y i| ≤ (volume {t | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp i t) ∈ B}).toReal / 2}.
Sibling results used, for compact B ⊆ ℝ^d and i ∈ Fin d:
(U) the slice length y ↦ (volume {t | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp i t) ∈ B}).toReal is upper semicontinuous [Submission.cbr_ci_iso_slice_length_usc];
(C) hence S_i(B) is compact [Submission.cbr_ci_iso_steiner_isCompact applied to (U)];
(V) if S_i(B) is measurable then L^d(S_i(B)) = L^d(B) [Submission.cbr_ci_iso_steiner_volume_eq]; this applies because a compact set is closed, hence measurable (IsCompact.measurableSet);
(D) ediam S_i(B) ≤ ediam B [Submission.cbr_ci_iso_steiner_ediam_le];
(R) R_i maps S_i(B) into itself, and for k ≠ i, if R_k maps B into itself then R_k maps S_i(B) into itself [Submission.cbr_ci_iso_steiner_reflection].
1. Claim: for every finite set F ⊆ Fin d there is a compact K_F with L^d(K_F) = L^d(A), ediam K_F ≤ ediam A, and R_k(x) ∈ K_F for all k ∈ F and x ∈ K_F. Proof by induction on F (Finset.induction_on).
2. F = ∅: take K_∅ := A; all properties are trivial.
3. Step from F' to F = insert i F' with i ∉ F'. Let K' := K_{F'} from the induction hypothesis and K := S_i(K'). By (U) and (C), K is compact. By (V) (K measurable as it is compact), L^d(K) = L^d(K') = L^d(A). By (D), ediam K ≤ ediam K' ≤ ediam A. For k ∈ F: if k = i, then R_i(K) ⊆ K by the first part of (R); if k ∈ F', then k ≠ i (because i ∉ F') and R_k(K') ⊆ K' by the induction hypothesis, so R_k(K) ⊆ K by the second part of (R).
4. Apply step 1 to F = Fin d (Finset.univ): K := K_univ is compact, L^d(K) = L^d(A), ediam K ≤ ediam A, and R_i(K) ⊆ K for every i ∈ Fin d.
5. Central symmetry. Fix x ∈ K. For a finite G ⊆ Fin d let x^G ∈ ℝ^d have coordinates (x^G)_k = −x_k if k ∈ G and x_k otherwise (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => if k ∈ G then −x k else x k)). By induction on G, x^G ∈ K. First, x^∅ = x ∈ K. Next, for i ∉ G, x^{insert i G} = R_i(x^G): coordinate i is −x_i = −(x^G)_i because i ∉ G, and the coordinates k ≠ i are unchanged. This point lies in K because x^G ∈ K and R_i(K) ⊆ K. For G = Fin d, x^G = −x (compare coordinates), so −x ∈ K.
6. K has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Finset induction over the processed coordinates, replacing K by S_i(K).

Each step preserves compactness (USC sibling plus compactness sibling), Lebesgue measure (volume sibling, measurable since compact), the diameter bound, and old reflection symmetries, and it adds R_i-symmetry.
After all coordinates, K is invariant under every R_i.
Flipping the coordinates one at a time gives −x ∈ K.

subproblem.title: Isodiametric inequality (Simon 2.10)
subproblem.statement: Isodiametric inequality: for every d ∈ ℕ and every set A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (not necessarily measurable or bounded), L^d(A) ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d in [0, ∞]. Here L^d = volume, ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and ediam is the extended diameter.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid d)), volume A ≤ unitBallVolume d * (ediam A / 2) ^ d
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 2.10 / parent steps 1a (reduction to compact sets) and 1g (conclusion).
1. ω_d ≠ 0: the open unit ball is nonempty and open, so its volume is positive (Metric.measure_ball_pos).
2. Case ediam A = ∞. Then d ≥ 1: for d = 0 every subset of the one-point space ℝ⁰ is subsingleton and has ediam 0 (ediam_subsingleton). Hence (ediam A/2)^d = (∞/2)^d = ∞ (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top, ENNReal.top_pow), the right-hand side is ω_d·∞ = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top), and the inequality holds.
3. Case ediam A < ∞ (reduction 1a). A is bounded (isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top), so its closure Ā is compact (Bornology.IsBounded.isCompact_closure; ℝ^d is proper). Moreover ediam Ā = ediam A (ediam_closure) and L^d(A) ≤ L^d(Ā) (monotonicity, A ⊆ Ā).
4. By the sibling Submission.cbr_ci_iso_exists_symmetric_replacement applied to the compact set Ā, there is a compact K with L^d(K) = L^d(Ā), ediam K ≤ ediam Ā = ediam A, and −x ∈ K for all x ∈ K.
5. By the sibling Submission.cbr_ci_iso_volume_le_of_neg_mem, L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d. Since t ↦ ω_d·(t/2)^d is monotone on [0, ∞] and ediam K ≤ ediam A, ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d (gcongr).
6. Hence L^d(A) ≤ L^d(Ā) = L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unbounded A: d ≥ 1 and the right-hand side is ∞.
Bounded A: pass to the compact closure, which has the same ediam and at least the same measure.
Replace the closure by a centrally symmetric compact set of equal measure and no larger ediam (symmetric_replacement).
Apply the centrally symmetric bound (symmetric_bound) and monotonicity in ediam.

subproblem.title: Lebesgue measure is at most (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d] on ℝ^d (completion of Simon 2.9)
subproblem.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ, the Lebesgue measure L^d = volume on ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is dominated by (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d]: L^d(s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s) for every set s ⊆ ℝ^d (as measures, L^d ≤ (ω_d/2^d)•μH[d]). Here ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and μH[d] is Mathlib's d-dimensional Hausdorff measure (weight diam^d, no normalising constant).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ), (volume : Measure (Euclid d)) ≤ (unitBallVolume d / 2 ^ d) • (μH[(d : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid d))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, 'Completion of the proof of 2.9' / parent step 2, translated to Mathlib's normalisation of μH[d].
1. Let c := ω_d/2^d. Then c ≠ 0, since ω_d ≠ 0 (Metric.measure_ball_pos) and 2^d ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.div_ne_zero). Also c ≠ ∞, since ω_d < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top) and 2^d ≠ 0 (ENNReal.div_ne_top).
2. For every set s ⊆ ℝ^d, the sibling isodiametric inequality Submission.cbr_ci_iso_volume_le_ediam_pow gives L^d(s) ≤ ω_d·(ediam s/2)^d = ω_d·ediam(s)^d·(2^d)⁻¹ = c·ediam(s)^d. The ENNReal arithmetic uses a/2 = a·2⁻¹ (div_eq_mul_inv), mul_pow, ENNReal.inv_pow and commutativity. Multiplying by c⁻¹: c⁻¹·L^d(s) ≤ c⁻¹·c·ediam(s)^d = ediam(s)^d (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, valid as c ∉ {0, ∞}).
3. Let ν := c⁻¹•L^d, a measure. By step 2, ν(s) ≤ ediam(s)^d = ediam(s)^(d : ℝ) for every set s (ENNReal.rpow_natCast). Hence ν ≤ μH[d]. Indeed, for any δ > 0 and any countable cover (C_k) of a set B by sets with ediam C_k ≤ δ, ν(B) ≤ Σ_k ν(C_k) ≤ Σ_k ediam(C_k)^d; taking the infimum over such covers and the supremum over δ > 0 gives ν(B) ≤ μH[d](B). In Mathlib this is exactly Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) ν 1 one_pos: its hypothesis is required only for sets of ediam ≤ 1, and step 2 gives it for all sets.
4. For every set s: L^d(s) = c·(c⁻¹·L^d(s)) = c·ν(s) ≤ c·μH[d](s) (ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel and monotonicity of multiplication). By the setwise characterisation of ≤ for measures (Measure.le_iff'), L^d ≤ c•μH[d]. ∎
proof_key_steps: c = ω_d/2^d is positive and finite.
The isodiametric inequality rewritten: L^d(s) ≤ c·ediam(s)^d, i.e. c⁻¹L^d(s) ≤ ediam(s)^d for all s.
Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure gives c⁻¹•L^d ≤ μH[d].
Multiplying back by c gives L^d ≤ c•μH[d] setwise.
